title: Mountain Training Arc (100K SPECIAL)
summary: 100K special filmed in his ancestral mountain village, training 10 days in a converted family smokehouse with minimal equipment and outdoor rings. He shares his specialization plans (less biceps/traps/chest, more forearms, triceps, lats, obliques) and an autobiographical story of overcoming mediocrity, a depressive relapse in college, and his commitment never to quit.
claims: He trains in his family's old smokehouse with a few rusty plates, dumbbells, one barbell and portable implements; the nearest gym is about 70 km away
Like a mountain, bodybuilding never ends: reach one goal and you see the next peak
After 15 years of training he still finds weaknesses to improve
A 10-day training block is not enough for significant gains but can prime the body for a new specialization
He has enough biceps, traps and chest, so they will take a back seat to lagging areas in coming years
Do not fully strip a body part of volume to bring up another; instead skew exercises toward the lagging area so the strong muscle still gets some work
Pronated curl variations still train biceps but shift stress to brachialis and brachioradialis; all his biceps volume on the trip is done that way
On the trip he trains arms in the morning and legs in the evening, like he did 10 years ago
Before bodybuilding he trained for football then basketball and ran in the mountains for hours each morning
Commercial gyms are optimal for muscle building, but training in nature feels more personal
Pull-ups are the best calisthenics movement for the back and one of his favorite exercises
He is fickle and drops what stops stimulating him, but is certain he will bodybuild for life
With little weight, do squats holding dumbbells with heels on an incline; even 50 lb per hand is hard in high reps
Everyone should go through a scarce-resource 'mountain training arc'; if you can train in a smokehouse you can train anywhere
He was small, unattractive and resentful as a kid; at 15 he started with 10 push-ups one day and curls the next, for two years
At 17 he got his first weight set and trained daily all summer with no rest days or deloads, plus morning runs
Conquering a steep hill on his bike, where he had always quit, marked his decision to stop quitting
Big arms come from commitment: pick isolation exercises you enjoy and blast them; for him it was always curls
His curl focus left an imbalance he now corrects by emphasizing forearms and triceps
Pronation twists load the brachioradialis and keep tension through the whole movement; only pronator fatigue stops him doing them every 48 hours
Without a cable machine, attach a resistance band to something and do triceps pushdowns
Stiff-legged variation gives unmatched hamstring stretch and likely trains middle and lower traps
Going forward his trap volume will come only from compound (non-isolation) work, with focus shifting to lats
You can never have too much abs, but you can skew work toward an area; he targets obliques with slow-tempo twisting sit-ups
After rejection by top universities he quit classes, played League of Legends 10 hours a day and stopped training for a year
Returning to the mountains and the smokehouse brought him back to training and out of depression
Self-worth should not depend on others' approval; you owe it to yourself to become your best version
exercises: Pull-ups on rings from a tree branch
challenging leg work without a barbell
shift biceps work to brachialis and brachioradialis
anchor band, push against an implement
huge hamstring stretch, upper back stimulus
